name: Sam
label: Shuffle-focused large-library listener
who: I keep very large playlists, often thousands of songs, and I mostly listen by shuffling them. I have cancelled Premium before and returned to free, and I compare the two mainly by how their shuffle behaves.
value_for_money: Felt free shuffle worked better than Premium shuffle [37]. Notes that Premium adds repeat and in-order play, while free has more ads [29]. Mentions price increases as one reason to consider switching [32].
loyalty: Stays because large playlists and saved songs would be hard to move [32][24]. Has left before, for YouTube [7] and by cancelling after 15 years [33]. Has also used an external reshuffler to re-shuffle playlists daily [13].
pain_points: Shuffle keeps replaying the same songs from large playlists
Smart shuffle inserts songs that are not in the playlist
Shuffle plays only a few artists' songs in a long playlist
Shuffle broke for free users after a recent update
likes: Autoplay after a single song works well
Daily random mode that works for them
reasons_to_stay: They keep a large liked-songs library and playlists on Spotify, including about 5,000 saved songs and a main playlist near 9,000 tracks [32][24]. They still value the recommendations when building playlists [5] and autoplay after a single song [12].
tone: Exasperated and detailed, venting about shuffle with caps and profanity.
